dataFlow: When a shopper submits the widget on a sold-out item, a signup row is inserted (deduped per email + item); on duplicate the widget confirms inline without a new row. When an inventory level rises above zero, the restock trigger resolves the inventory item to its variant and product, looks up all waitlisted signups for that item ordered by signup time, determines the batch size from config, marks the batch as notified (creating a notification_batch row as the restock event record), and enqueues an email per subscriber in that batch; subscribers beyond the batch size remain queued for the next restock. Each email carries a per-signup unsubscribe token and product/variant context fetched live at send time. When an order is paid, the system checks whether any notified subscribers for each purchased variant converted, recording the conversion so the merchant can see "demand recovered" metrics. When a product is deleted, all associated signups and notification batches are soft-deleted. The admin dashboard reads from a pre-aggregated stats snapshot refreshed on every notification batch completion and on every conversion event, so all dashboard metrics are served at the same latency.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update fires for the same restock — the notification_batch keyed by item_external_id + restock_date_bucket deduplicates it; the second delivery exits before selecting any signups or sending any emails.

Inventory briefly spikes then drops again before all emails are dispatched — signups already marked notified in the batch remain notified; the next restock starts a fresh batch for remaining pending signups only.

Partial restock with fewer available units than waitlisted shoppers — only the front-of-queue batch_size signups are notified; the rest stay pending and are picked up on the next restock event, so the batch size config should reflect the merchant's available unit count.

Shopper signs up for the same item from the same email twice — the unique constraint on (email, item_external_id) makes the second insert a no-op; the widget confirms inline without creating a new row.

Notification email delivery fails permanently for a subscriber — the notification_send is marked failed; the signup is NOT re-queued for the same batch cycle but retains notified status so it is excluded from the next batch for that same restock.

Product title or variant name changes in Shopify between restock events — demand_stats_snapshot titles are known-stale until the next batch completion or conversion triggers a snapshot refresh; this is the accepted staleness window and is bounded by the next event.
